title: Silent Hill
full_review:
Based on a video game, director Christophe Gans' bleak and surreal supernatural thriller "Silent Hill" (TriStar) is about a mother (Radha Mitchell) whose desperate search for her missing daughter (Jodelle Ferland) leads her to a ghost town -- ravaged by fire 30 years earlier -- where she faces demonic forces and the town's dark past to get her child back.

Suffused with religious motifs, Gans' journey through hell abounds with nightmarish visions worthy of Dante. But in exploring themes of faith, fanaticism and motherhood, the film, which starts out eerily intriguing, eventually descends into confusion and gore. Its perplexing ending will leave you, like the haunted hamlet, in a fog.

The film contains intensely disturbing and bloody horror images, including a graphic scene of a woman burned alive, some violence, including a savage off-screen beating, fleeting partial nudity, and recurring rough and crude language and profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
